**Original model announcement text (primary post by @claudeai):**  
"Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5, the second model in the Claude 5.5 family.

It’s a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5, runs more than 30% faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work."

**Timestamp of the original post:** Mon, 28 Sep 2026 18:03:31 GMT (post ID: 2104633115620823187).[[1]](https://x.com/i/status/2104633115620823187)

This is the primary post in the thread. All subsequent posts in the thread (IDs 2104633119412523294 through 2104633140409192757, timestamps 18:03:32–18:03:37 GMT) are also authored by **Claude - @claudeai** (the official account). They form a continuous self-thread expanding on benchmarks, speed, cost, use cases, alignment, and availability.

**Does it explicitly say "Claude Sonnet 5.5 is live"?** No.  
- The primary post introduces the model but does not state that it is live, available, or released.  
- The final self-reply in the thread (ID: 2104633140409192757, timestamp: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 18:03:37 GMT) does say: "Claude Sonnet 5.5 is available everywhere today." This is primary-post evidence from the same author, but it is not in the original announcement post itself. Per the query, only primary-post evidence is considered; no inference from dates or later replies is used.

**Distinction from replies by other accounts:**  
The only non-@claudeai reply shown in the fetched thread is from **𝕱𝖚𝖑𝖑 𝕶𝖊𝖑𝖑𝖞 - @full_kelly_** (post ID: 2104633378461057531, timestamp: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 18:04:34 GMT). Its content is unrelated to the announcement ("we should slow down AI anyway, here’s Opus 5.5 update: here’s Sonnet 5.5") and is clearly a reply by a different account. No other external replies were needed for this analysis; only one X search call (the thread fetch) was used.
